stem: A resident investor (not a promoter) tenders shares in a company buyback in June 2026. How are the proceeds taxed?
options: Entirely as dividend at slab rates, with cost becoming a separate capital loss
As capital gains: proceeds minus cost, short- or long-term by holding period
Fully exempt because the company has already paid buyback tax
As business income at a flat 30%
why: Finance Act 2026 omitted s.2(40)(f) and rewrote s.69: buyback proceeds are capital gains from 1 April 2026.

stem: From tax year 2026-27, an investor who borrowed to buy dividend-paying shares wants to deduct the loan interest from dividend income. What does the law allow?
options: No deduction at all against dividend or mutual fund income
Interest up to 20% of the dividend
The full interest, as dividend is income from other sources
Interest up to 2 lakh a year
why: FA 2026 substituted s.93(2): no deduction against dividend or MF income.

stem: An individual bought Sovereign Gold Bonds on the stock exchange in 2024 and holds them to maturity. Is the redemption gain exempt from 2026?
options: Yes; redemption by any individual is exempt
Yes, but only if held for more than three years
No; SGB gains are always taxed at slab rates
No; the exemption now applies only to an individual who held the bond from original issue to maturity
why: s.70(1)(x) as substituted by FA 2026 limits the exemption to holding from original issue till maturity.

stem: What is the securities transaction tax on the sale of an option (on the premium) after the Finance Act 2026?
why: FA 2026 s.159 raised it from 0.1% to 0.15%.

stem: After the Finance Act 2026, STT on the sale of a futures contract is:
why: FA 2026 s.159: futures from 0.02% to 0.05%.

stem: A promoter that is a domestic company earns a long-term gain in a buyback in 2026. Besides normal capital gains tax, what additional tax applies?
options: An additional 9.5% on the long-term gain
An additional 17.5% on the long-term gain
No additional tax for domestic-company promoters
An additional 2% on the long-term gain
why: New s.69(2) table: LTCG additional 9.5% for a domestic-company promoter, 17.5% otherwise.

stem: STT on an option that is exercised, after the Finance Act 2026, is:
Which statement about a buyback that took place in December 2025 is correct?
options: It is taxed as capital gains because the 2026 change is retrospective
It is exempt in the shareholder's hands
It follows the October 2024 rule: the amount is a dividend and the cost becomes a capital loss
It is taxed at a flat 20% as a special-rate income
why: The FA 2026 change applies from 1 April 2026; earlier buybacks keep the 2024 treatment.

stem: Under the Income-tax Act 2025, income earned between 1 April 2026 and 31 March 2027 is taxed for:
why: s.3: tax year is the financial year; the previous/assessment year pair is gone.

stem: Under the new regime for 2026-27, what is the tax rate on the slice of income between 12 lakh and 16 lakh (before rebate and cess)?
A resident individual under the new regime has total income of 12.05 lakh (no special-rate income). What is the maximum tax payable before cess, given marginal relief?
why: s.156(2)(b): tax limited to the excess over 12 lakh, i.e. 5,000.

stem: Under the old regime for 2026-27, a resident aged 70 pays no tax on income up to:
why: FA 2026 Part III Paragraph A(II): nil up to 3 lakh for 60-79.

stem: Which deduction remains available under the new tax regime?
options: Interest on a loan for a self-occupied house
why: s.202(2)(a)(xii) excepts the s.124 employer NPS contribution.

stem: For an individual on the new regime with total income of 3.5 crore (all salary), the surcharge rate is:
why: New-regime income has no 37% band; above 2 crore it is 25%.

stem: An Indian citizen visiting India from abroad, with Indian income of 20 lakh, is in India 130 days this year and 400 days over the previous four years. Their status is:
options: Deemed resident only if not taxed abroad
why: s.6(5): the 60-day test becomes 120 days for visitors with Indian income above 15 lakh; s.6(13)(b) makes them RNOR.

stem: What is the standard deduction for a salaried taxpayer under the new regime?
why: s.19 Table item 2: 75,000 where tax is computed under s.202(1).

stem: Listed equity shares are sold after 14 months with STT paid on purchase and sale. The long-term gain is taxed at:
options: 12.5% on the whole gain with indexation
12.5% on gains above 1.25 lakh in the year
why: s.198: 12.5% above 1.25 lakh.

stem: A resident individual sells a flat bought in 2016 in tax year 2026-27. What choice do they have for the long-term gain?
options: 12.5% without indexation or 20% with indexation, whichever tax is lower
Slab rates on the indexed gain
why: s.197(3) for land/building acquired before 23 July 2024 by resident individuals/HUF.

stem: Units of a debt fund that holds 80% in debt, bought in August 2023 and sold in 2027, produce:
options: Short-term gains at slab rates, whatever the holding
why: s.76: specified mutual fund (more than 65% debt) bought from 1 April 2023.

stem: Shares bought in 2015 at 100 had a highest quoted price of 180 on 31 January 2018 and are sold at 150 in 2026. The cost for the long-term gain is:
why: Grandfathering: higher of actual cost and the lower of the 31 Jan 2018 value and sale price = 150.

stem: How many houses can an individual buy with a 1.8 crore long-term gain from selling a house and still claim the house-to-house exemption?
options: Two, every time the gain is below 2 crore
Two, but only once in a lifetime
why: s.82(5): two houses once, if the gain does not exceed 2 crore.

stem: What is the maximum that can be invested in specified bonds to save tax on land or building gains?
why: s.85(2): 50 lakh across the tax year and the next.

stem: An investor takes a loan against the specified bonds bought to save capital gains tax, two years after buying them. What happens?
options: Nothing, because the bonds are still held
The exempted gain becomes taxable in the year of the loan
Only the interest on the bonds becomes taxable
why: s.85(4): a loan on the security of the bonds is treated as converting them into money.

stem: A long-term capital loss on gold can be set off against:
options: Any capital gain, short or long

stem: For how many tax years can an unabsorbed capital loss be carried forward?
An individual owns two houses and sells listed shares for a large long-term gain. Can they claim the any-asset-to-house exemption on buying a third house?
options: Yes, if all the sale proceeds are reinvested
Yes, but only up to 50 lakh
No; it is unavailable if they own more than one house other than the new one on the sale date
Yes, if the new house is under construction

stem: A person receives cash gifts of 30,000 from a friend and 40,000 from a colleague in one tax year. How much is taxable?
options: Nothing, as each gift is below 50,000
why: s.92(2)(m): once the total from non-relatives exceeds 50,000, the whole amount is taxable.

stem: Which of these gifts is taxable in the recipient's hands?
options: 2 lakh from a friend on the recipient's birthday
10 lakh from an uncle on the recipient's wedding
A flat inherited from a grandparent
why: Relatives, marriage and inheritance are exempt; a friend is not a relative.

stem: Under the old regime, the maximum interest deduction on a loan for a self-occupied house completed within five years is:
options: 2 lakh a year, including pre-construction interest instalments
2 lakh a year, plus pre-construction interest without limit
why: s.22(2) as amended by FA 2026 to cover s.22(1)(b) and (c).

stem: A husband gifts 20 lakh to his wife, who invests it in a fixed deposit. The FD interest is taxed in the hands of:
options: Neither, as it is a gift
why: s.99(1): income from assets transferred to a spouse without adequate consideration is clubbed.

stem: The overall limit for old-regime deductions for PPF, ELSS, life insurance and home-loan principal is:
why: s.123 with Schedule XV.

stem: Under the old regime, a taxpayer aged 40 pays health insurance premiums for self and for parents aged 65. The maximum deduction is:
why: s.126: 25,000 for self/family plus 50,000 for senior-citizen parents.

stem: Under the old regime, a resident senior citizen may deduct interest on bank deposits up to:
why: s.153 (formerly 80TTB).

stem: A minor child earns interest on an FD gifted by the parents; the parents are married and the father's income is higher. The interest is taxed in:
why: s.99: clubbed with the parent whose income is greater.

stem: A salaried individual has an F&O loss in tax year 2026-27. Which statement is correct?
options: It can be set off against salary
It is a speculative loss carried forward four years
It can only be set off against capital gains
It can be set off against any income except salary and carried forward eight years
why: F&O is non-speculative business income (s.2(31)); s.109, s.112.

stem: Losses from intraday equity trading can be carried forward for:
options: Eight tax years, against any business income
Eight tax years, against capital gains
Four tax years, against speculative income only

stem: A trader's turnover is 6 crore and cash receipts and payments are each under 5% of the total. Is a tax audit required on turnover grounds?
options: No; the threshold is 10 crore in this case
Only if the trader claims a loss
why: s.63 table: 1 crore, raised to 10 crore with cash within 5%.

stem: A loss on selling a cryptocurrency can be:
options: Neither set off nor carried forward
Set off against gains on other cryptocurrencies
Set off against capital gains on shares
why: s.194 bars set-off and carry-forward of VDA losses.

stem: By 15 September, what share of the year's estimated advance tax must have been paid?
why: Advance tax table: 15% / 45% / 75% / 100%.

stem: An NRI has income of 6 lakh in India, all short-term gains on listed shares. Which relief is NOT available to them?
options: Paying tax at 20% on the gains
Claiming a refund of excess TDS
Using the unused basic exemption limit against the gains
Treaty relief with a tax residency certificate
why: The basic-exemption shortfall adjustment in s.196(2) is for residents only.

stem: Under SEBI rules, the maximum fixed fee an investment adviser may charge an individual client's family per year is:
why: Master Circular for IAs para 1(iii)(b).

stem: An investment adviser may charge an individual client fees in advance for at most:
options: The full term of the agreement
why: Master Circular para 1(iii)(h).

stem: A client ends advisory services after four months of a one-year prepaid fee. The adviser must:
options: Refund the unexpired period, keeping at most one quarter's fee as a break fee
Refund nothing, as the fee was prepaid
Refund the unexpired period with no deduction
why: Master Circular para 1(iii)(h).

stem: An existing advisory client of an RIA asks to buy a regular-plan mutual fund through the adviser's group distribution arm. What applies?
options: Permitted if the commission is disclosed
Permitted for mutual funds but not for PMS
Permitted if the client signs a waiver, whatever their profile
Not permitted: a client can take either advice or distribution within the group, not both
why: Reg. 22(5) and Master Circular para 1(i); a waiver is only for institutional or accredited clients.

stem: Which information must an investment adviser collect for risk profiling under Regulation 16?
options: Only the client's stated risk appetite
Age, objectives and horizon, income, existing assets, risk appetite and liabilities
why: Reg. 16(a).

stem: An RIA uses an AI chatbot to generate recommendations for clients. What do the regulations require?
options: Nothing, as long as a human reviews the output
Disclose the extent of AI use to clients; the adviser remains solely responsible for the advice and data
Prior approval from SEBI for each AI tool
Only that clients pay a lower fee

stem: An adviser recommends a stock on Monday. For how long may it not trade on its own account against that advice without first giving clients a revised view?
Which may an RIA include in an advertisement?
options: A disclaimer that registration does not guarantee performance or returns
why: Master Circular para 10.

stem: If the adviser does not resolve a client's complaint, the client can next approach:
options: SEBI's SCORES portal, which links to online dispute resolution
why: Master Circular para 6.

stem: For how long must an investment adviser keep records of advice-related interactions?
options: Five years, or longer if a dispute is pending
One year after the agreement ends
why: Master Circular para 1(xiii)C.

stem: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations 2026, the maximum exit load an open-ended scheme may charge is:
Under the 2026 regulations, the base expense ratio cap for an index fund or ETF is:
Which cost is excluded from a mutual fund's base expense ratio under the 2026 regulations?
options: GST and exchange or regulatory transaction costs
why: Reg. 66(7) excludes statutory levies and transaction costs.

stem: Under the 2026 categorisation rules, a fund house offering both a value fund and a contra fund must ensure that:
options: Only one is open to new investors
Their portfolios overlap by no more than 50%
They invest in different market-cap segments
why: Master Circular para 3.8.1(d).

stem: A life cycle fund charges an exit load on redemption in the second year of investment of:
why: Master Circular Annexure 1B para 3.

stem: The minimum investment in a Specialized Investment Fund for a non-accredited investor is:
options: 10 lakh across the fund house's SIF strategies
why: Master Circular chapter 21.

stem: A redemption request for an equity fund is accepted on a business day. The proceeds must reach the investor within:
why: Master Circular para 15.3.1.

stem: In the first year, the maximum exit load a portfolio manager may charge on redemption is:
why: PMS Master Circular para 6.1.4.

stem: An RIA's client invests in a Category II AIF. Which plan must the client be onboarded into?
options: The regular plan, with trail commission only
The direct plan, with no distribution fee
Either plan, at the client's choice
The plan with one-third upfront commission
why: AIF Master Circular para 16.1.2.

stem: A SEBI-registered research analyst may charge an individual client's family at most, per year:
why: RA Master Circular fee provisions.
